newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: INTERVIEW-Aerolineas to pick partner for expansion.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Aerolineas to pick partner for expansion.

text.p: The main shareholders of Aerolineas Argentinas will pick a U.S. partner this month and then launch an expansion plan with investments of $700 million to $1.0 billion, the company's president Manuel Moran said.
"The new partner will be announced no later than this month," Moran told Reuters in an interview earlier this week. "It may be even a matter of days."

He added AMR Corp or Continental Airlines Inc will be sold a 10 percent stake in Interinvest, the entity that controls the former Argentine state-run carrier currently operated by Spains's state-owned Iberia Lineas
"Then Iberia will swap the 20 percent stake it has in Aerolineas for a 10 percent stake in Interinvest," he said in the interview Tuesday.
"The remaining 80 percent of Interinvest will be sold among investment funds, local shareholders and financial institutions."
Interinvest, owner of 63.35 percent of Aerolineas, was formed by the Spanish state (40 percent), Merrill Lynch and Co Inc (45 percent) and Bankers Trust New York Corp (15 percent).
The Argentine state owns five percent of Aerolineas, the company's employees have a 10 percent stake and the remaining 1.65 percent is the hands of Argentine private investors.
Under the new share structure Iberia would no longer be the single operator of Aerolineas, South America's second largest carrier after Brazil's Varig, Moran said.

"Interinvest shareholders and the rest of Aerolineas shareholders will name a new board who in turn will name a new management," he said. "The most convenient model is that the operation of Aerolineas be shared by Iberia and the new U.S. partner...and, of course, local shareholders."
Moran headed a three-year recovery plan under which Aerolineas went from losing $150 million in 1993 to a projected slight operating profit this year.

"Once the new partner is chosen we will launch a process that has been delayed, basically -- the development of the U.S. market," he said. "Our expectations there are for an increase of 30 to 40 percent in seat capacity."

In order to do that, he said, Aerolineas has to enter into code sharing agreements and explore the posssibility of opening new gateways into the United States. It currently flies to Los Angeles, New York and Miami.
"The new board will have to decide on an investment plan to renew the long range fleet and within months to replace all the medium and short range fleet," Moran said.
"This kind of decision has to be taken at the highest level as they may imply investments that can easily reach $700 million or $1.0 billion."
Aerolineas has 34 airplanes, among them six long range Boeing 747s and three Airbus 310-300s. It also has 17 Boeing 737s and seven MD88s.
The new partner would get wider acces to the South American market, where Aerolineas has a 36 market share.
The company also has a 31 percent market share of all flights between Argentina and the United States and 34 percent of all flights between Argentina and Europe.
Aerolineas and its local sister carrier Austral each has a 38 percent market share of the Argentine domestic market.
Moran said the company also plans an increase in its seat capacity to Europe by about 15 to 20 percent.
The plan also implies the total renewal of Austral's fleet, which includes six MD80s and six DC9s. Austral is 90 percent controlled by Interinvest and also headed by Moran.
Aerolineas has a 10 percent stake in Austral that in a matter of weeks or even days will be totally sold to Austral's employees, Moran said.

He added Aerolineas also expects to increase its cargo factor, which currently accounts for 10 percent of all its revenue. "We aim to an about 15 percent increase and in a few years to reach 20 percent."
Aerolineas has a net worth of $335 million resulting from $987 million in assets and $652 million in liabilities.
((--Buenos Aires newsroom, 541 318-0650--))
